Network Inspector CLI

Usage: ni <command> [options]

Commands:
  convert   Convert capture files between formats (frame-level)
  export    Parse and export packets to analysis formats

Use 'ni <command> --help' for more information about a command.

result.stderr:
Usage: ni convert <sources...> -o <output> [options]

Convert capture files between formats (frame-level, no protocol parsing).

Arguments:
  <sources...>          One or more source files or specs

Options:
  -o, --output          Output file path (required; '-' for stdout)
  --output-format, -f   Output format spec (see below; overrides extension)
  -n, --max-frames      Maximum number of frames to convert
  --split-size <MB>     Split output at this size in MiB
  --split-count <N>     Split output every N frames
  --profile <name>      Settings profile name
  --settings-path <dir> Base directory for settings storage
  --blf-cache-size <MB> Container cache budget for BLF sources (MiB)
  --progress <N>        Report progress every N frames
  --tolerant            Skip malformed frames instead of aborting
  -h, --help            Show this help message

Output format is auto-detected from the output extension:
  .pcapng / other       PCAPNG (default)
  .blf                  BLF with default compression

Output format specifications (--output-format):
  pcapng                PCAPNG format
  blf                   BLF, default compression
  blf:compression=off   BLF, no compression
  blf:compression=fast  BLF, fast compression
  blf:compression=best  BLF, best compression ratio

Source specifications:
  capture.pcap[ng]      Auto-detected PCAP/PCAPNG
  data.blf              Auto-detected BLF
  pcap:path=<file>      Explicit PCAP/PCAPNG spec
  blf:path=<file>       Explicit BLF spec
  random:count=N,seed=S,mode=udp4|udp6|random  Synthetic frames

Examples:
  ni convert capture.pcap -o output.pcapng
  ni convert input.blf -o output.pcapng --progress 1000
  ni convert input.pcap -o output.blf --output-format blf:compression=best
  ni convert big.pcapng -o split.pcapng --split-count 10000
  ni convert big.blf -o out.pcapng --blf-cache-size 256 --split-size 512

result.stderr:
Usage: ni export <sources...> [options]

Parse and export packets to analysis formats.

Arguments:
  <sources...>          One or more source files or specs

Options:
  -o, --output          Output file path ('-' or omit for stdout)
  -f, --format          Export format spec (see below)
  -n, --max-packets     Maximum number of packets to export
  --profile <name>      Settings profile name
  --settings-path <dir> Base directory for settings storage
  --blf-cache-size <MB> Container cache budget for BLF sources (MiB)
  --progress <N>        Report progress every N packets
  --tolerant            Skip malformed frames instead of aborting
  -h, --help            Show this help message

Source specifications:
  capture.pcap[ng]      Auto-detected PCAP/PCAPNG file
  data.blf              Auto-detected BLF file
  pcap:path=<file>      Explicit PCAP/PCAPNG spec
  blf:path=<file>       Explicit BLF spec
  random:count=N,seed=S,mode=udp4|udp6|random  Synthetic frames

Format specifications:
  json                  Compact JSON (default for stdout / .json)
  json:style=compact    Compact JSON
  json:style=pretty     Pretty-printed JSON
  json:style=array      JSON array format
  pbf                   Standard PBF
  pbf:format=standard   Standard (row-oriented) PBF
  pbf:format=columnar   Columnar PBF
  pbf:format=columnar,compressed  Columnar PBF with LZ4
  text                  Human-readable protocol tree (default for .txt)
  text:level=summary    Protocol containers only (no field values)
  text:level=standard   All fields except raw bytes (default)
  text:level=full       All fields including raw bytes
  text:truncate=N       Truncate values at N characters (0 = unlimited, default: 256)
  text:level=full,truncate=0  Full detail without any truncation

Examples:
  ni export capture.pcap -o output.json -f json:style=pretty
  ni export input.pcap -o data.pbf -f pbf:format=columnar,compressed
  ni export input.pcap -o output.json -n 100 --progress 10
  ni export random:count=1000,mode=udp4 -f json
  ni export capture.pcap
[truncated]
